correctness.evidence: Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies the base expansion, both parity-dependent splitting identities, odd/distinct/strictly-larger children, and the stated first five maxima. The lcm/p-adic congruence proof of the prime-power obstruction is valid.

originality.evidence: Elsholtz arXiv:1606.02117 proves that for all sufficiently large odd k there are many distinct-odd-denominator representations of 1, which already forces infinitely many odd largest denominators. Martin's Denser Egyptian Fractions explicitly notes the earlier Erdős–Graham observation that prime powers cannot be largest denominators.

value.evidence: After prior coverage is acknowledged, the residual is an elementary alternative construction/proof and sample sequence, without a new classification, density result, quantitative improvement, or structural regime.

literature.title: Egyptian Fractions with odd denominators
literature.author: Christian Elsholtz
literature.coverage: Positive doubly-exponential lower bounds for the number of distinct odd-denominator representations of 1 for sufficiently large odd k; this implies unbounded and hence infinitely many odd largest denominators.

literature.title: Denser Egyptian Fractions
literature.author: Greg Martin
literature.coverage: Studies the Erdős–Graham largest-denominator exceptional set; full text states the earlier observation that a prime power can never be the largest denominator in an Egyptian-fraction representation of 1.

literature.title: OEIS A260402
literature.coverage: Sequence of numbers that cannot be largest denominators; explicitly notes inclusion of all primes and prime powers and cites Martin.

repair.reason: Reframing as an elementary constructive proof would be accurate but would not provide a novel or sufficiently substantive scientific result after the stronger prior coverage is acknowledged.

final_reason: The mathematics is correct, but both existential conclusions are already covered by prior work, leaving only an elementary alternative construction and reproof without sufficient residual scientific value.
